name: Kamala Harris
role: Former U.S. vice president (2021–2025); 2024 Democratic presidential nominee; U.S. senator from California (2017–2021)
summary: Harris is a Democratic centre-left liberal, shaped by a prosecutor's career in San Francisco and California. She backs abortion rights, same-sex marriage, gun restrictions, higher taxes on the wealthy, unions and climate action, and wants criminal justice and policing reform. In 2024 she moved toward the centre on fracking, single-payer health care and the border, and she supports NATO, Ukraine and Israel's right to defend itself while pressing for a Gaza ceasefire and two states.

universal-healthcare.rationale: In 2019 she called health care 'a fundamental right' to be delivered through Medicare for All (a single payer with a 10-year transition). In 2024 she said she no longer backs single payer but that access to health care 'should be a right and not just a privilege', and she would strengthen the Affordable Care Act and private options; the latest position is a softer yes.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Backs raising the federal minimum wage (2024 campaign), without naming a figure; in 2019 she said a minimum-wage job 'does not pay enough' and she co-sponsored the Be HEARD Act to end the tipped minimum wage.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Says 'I believe in capitalism, but capitalism is not working for most people' and calls herself a pragmatic capitalist; she backs both competitive markets and extensive government correction, so no clear answer either way.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: 2019: 'people who are making $10 million a year... need to pay more taxes' and repeal of the 2017 tax cuts for the top 1 percent. 2024: restoring the 28 percent corporate rate, a higher capital gains rate, a billionaire minimum tax.

unions-good.rationale: Launched her 2019 campaign for an America 'where any worker can join a union', co-sponsored the Workplace Democracy Act, and condemned rhetoric calling unions 'special-interest groups'.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Prosecuted big banks, for-profit colleges and pharma as attorney general, proposed fining firms for pay gaps, a federal ban on price gouging, and in 2023 said that without strong oversight 'some technology companies choose to prioritize profit' over the public.

cut-welfare.rationale: Her record runs the opposite way: bills to expand SNAP by 30 percent and to send monthly payments during the pandemic, the expanded child tax credit, and her LIFT tax credit; she has not argued that welfare breeds dependency.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Supports legalising marijuana for adults federally (MORE Act, 'legalize marijuana' in 2019) and says 'we don't need another War on Drugs', but she has not backed legalising other recreational drugs.

limit-guns.rationale: Backs universal background checks, a ban on assault weapons, mandatory buybacks (2019) and executive action against dealers who break the law, while saying 'we're not taking anybody's guns away' and that she owns a gun.

empower-police-military.rationale: Points both ways: 'strongest, most lethal fighting force' and more border agents, but also wants police reform, body cameras and independent investigations, and said in 2020 that LAPD budgets deserved re-examination.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Mixed: opposed a 2008 San Francisco measure to decriminalise sex work and prosecuted Backpage, but in 2019 told The Root she favoured decriminalising it ('I think so. I do') while prioritising arrests of pimps and buyers.

decide-locally.rationale: Argued that when states fail on civil rights 'the federal government must step in', proposed Justice Department pre-clearance of state abortion laws, and favoured federal legislation on guns, health care and abortion.

rehabilitation.rationale: Created a re-entry and job-training programme as district attorney and says she wants to end mass incarceration, end solitary confinement and close for-profit prisons; voted for the First Step Act.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: As California attorney general she refused to defend Proposition 8, ordered marriages to start after it fell, and officiated at the plaintiffs' wedding; her 2024 convention speech names 'the freedom to love who you love'.

abortion-legal.rationale: Says she 'absolutely support[s] reinstating the protections of Roe v. Wade' and would sign a bill restoring them; 'the freedom to make decisions about one's own body should not be made by the government'.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Argues the federal government 'must step in' where states fail on civil rights, backs the Equality Act, and highlights racial gaps in maternal deaths, pay and sentencing as injustices to be fixed.

free-trade.rationale: Mixed: says 'I am not a protectionist Democrat... we need to sell our stuff' and wants 'fair trade', but opposed TPP, NAFTA and USMCA.

nation-first.rationale: Mixed: stresses alliances and global leadership ('we strengthen, not abdicate') yet frames goals as American interests ('America, not China, wins the competition for the 21st century').

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Called climate a 'climate crisis... an existential threat to us as a species', backed the Green New Deal and a $10 trillion plan for 100 percent clean power by 2030; in 2024 she kept the same urgency, pointing to the Inflation Reduction Act.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Called Trump's tariffs a 'trade tax' that hurt farmers and manufacturers and opposed his 2024 import tax; she said 'I am not a protectionist Democrat'. She wants fair trade rather than tariff protection.

democracy-best.rationale: Frames the choice as 'democracy and tyranny', pledges to hold 'sacred' free and fair elections and the peaceful transfer of power, and conceded the 2024 election she lost.

political-violence-never.rationale: Said 'we are never going to condone violence' while backing peaceful protest, and called the January 6 attack on the Capitol an incitement to violence against democracy.

military-superiority.rationale: 'As commander in chief, I will ensure America always has the strongest, most lethal fighting force in the world.'

results-over-ideology.rationale: Promised a president who is 'realistic, practical, and has common sense' and says her values lead to pragmatic, workable policy.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Wrote in 2019 that peace requires 'two states for two peoples', opposed West Bank annexation, and says she has supported Israel and its right to defend itself throughout her career.

national-self-determination.rationale: Stated that 'people have a right to choose their own form of government' and 'nations have a right to choose their own alliances', and backs Palestinian 'self-determination' through two states.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Mixed: 2019 plan ended support for oil and gas projects and she backed a fracking ban, but in 2024 she dropped the ban and cited 'the largest increase in domestic oil production in history'.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Pledged independent investigations and a revived Civil Rights Division after police killings such as Eric Garner's, and backed accountability for police; this concerns domestic police rather than past state abuses generally.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Says her work is about 'the dignity of all people' and an America with 'equal treatment, collective purpose and freedom for all'; 'equal justice under law' is the ideal she invokes.

separated-powers.rationale: Praises the framers for designing 'checks and balances' ('our framers then rightly designed our system of democracy to say there will be checks and balances'), citing impeachment.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Says 'we are a diverse country, and it's part of our strength' and that Americans have 'so much more in common than what separates us', rejecting the idea that diversity divides.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Introduced the Price Gouging Prevention Act (2020), which treats price rises over 10 percent in a declared emergency as gouging, and in 2024 proposed a federal ban on grocery price gouging; this is a cap on emergency price increases rather than a fixed price.

party-controls-media.rationale: Condemned leaders who 'attack a free press' (2019 launch) and warned of an 'explicit intent to jail journalists' (2024).

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Argues NATO and other alliances are central to security and attacked Trump for threatening to abandon NATO; she wants to strengthen them, not end them.

death-penalty.rationale: 'I am personally opposed to the death penalty. I've always been opposed'; she called the federal resumption of executions 'immoral' and co-sponsored a 2019 bill to ban it. As attorney general she still defended California's law in court.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: In 2019 said she was open to abolishing the Electoral College because the popular vote 'has been diminished', but framed it as open to discussion.

collective-defense.rationale: 'America's commitment to Article 5 is ironclad. This commitment is sacrosanct to me'; NATO is 'the greatest military alliance the world has ever seen'.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Condemned Russia's annexation of Crimea as a 'severe violation of the international norms' and says 'national borders should not be changed by force'; she supports Ukraine's territorial integrity.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Wants higher earners to pay more: 'people who are making $10 million a year... need to pay more taxes'; her tax proposals raise rates at the top, the opposite of one flat rate.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: 'No one is above the law, including the president of the United States.'

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Opposed the TPP for weak worker and environmental protection, said she would not have voted for NAFTA, voted against USMCA over climate, and says trade policy must 'protect workers... protect the environment'.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: As attorney general she filed an amicus brief in Fisher v. University of Texas urging the Court to let public universities consider race as one factor, and opposed California's ban on affirmative action.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Says federal law must step in where states fail on civil rights, citing the Civil Rights Act and the Voting Rights Act, and that 'we need to pass the Equality Act', which bars private discrimination.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Signed a letter to the defense secretary protesting 'the overt politicization of the military' by border deployments and warned of a president who would 'deploy our active-duty military against our own citizens'.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: No recorded position. Pledges to protect Social Security from cuts are a related issue; she did not address private individual pension accounts.

corporate-influence.rationale: Her 2019 campaign refused corporate PAC and lobbyist money ('a very deliberate choice') and she described bankers' 'arrogance of power'.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Her Open Justice data portal and her use of FOIA to seek Trump-Ukraine records show support for access to government information; she has not framed it as a legal right.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Her marriage-equality record and her 2024 speech championing 'the freedom to love who you love openly and with pride' put her against criminalising same-sex relations, though she has not spoken on foreign criminal laws.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Warned of a leader intent on jailing 'journalists, political opponents, and anyone he sees as the enemy', calling that outside American values.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Pledged to pass the Equality Act, introduced the Gay and Trans Panic Defense Prohibition Act, and told the ACLU in 2019 she backed gender-transition care for people in custody; in 2024 she spoke of following the law, and as attorney general she opposed such care for a state inmate.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Reintroduced the EMPOWER Act with Sen. Murkowski to bar harassment-silencing nondisclosure clauses and signed the Be HEARD Act, which ends mandatory arbitration and pre-employment NDAs.

social-market-economy.rationale: Describes an economy where government must act 'aggressively to foster competition and correct distortions' (price-gouging ban, corporate tax, antitrust-style housing bills) alongside a social safety net, while rejecting socialism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Calls for 'the strongest, most lethal fighting force in the world' and a duty to care for troops, leaving no room for disbanding the armed forces.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Commits the United States to NATO and to defending allies against Russian aggression, and warns Trump would let 'Putin sitting in Kyiv', rather than keep out of blocs.

open-government-data.rationale: As attorney general she launched Open Justice, publishing data on deaths in custody and arrest rates by race; she also led a FOIA suit over the Ukraine documents.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: As a prosecutor she calls for police and prison reform ('bad cops are bad for good cops'), shutting for-profit prisons and ending cash bail, not abolishing police or prisons, and she attacked Trump for wanting to defund federal law enforcement.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Calls climate change and AI misuse 'existential' threats that demand global action, but does not rank extinction risk as the top priority.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Wants Congress to rewrite the war authorisation and ended 'endless wars', but would act on an 'imminent threat' and backed arming Ukraine; the evidence points both ways.

free-public-college.rationale: Said she supports 'debt-free college' and backed a plan to pay tuition at public colleges for families earning up to $125,000, which is partial rather than universal free tuition.

future-generations.rationale: Describes climate action through her nieces and 'our children and our grandchildren': 'all children need to be able to breathe clean air and drink clean water'.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Co-sponsored the Workplace Democracy Act, which makes it easier for workers to form unions and bargain; she lists union-won benefits and wants workers to be able to renegotiate contracts through their unions.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Her LIFT Act would give families earning under $100,000 a tax credit of up to $6,000 a year (up to $500 a month); in 2024 she proposed a $6,000 child tax credit in a baby's first year.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Proposed cancelling up to $20,000 of debt for Pell Grant recipients who start a business in a disadvantaged area, and as vice president supported the administration's debt relief.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: No recorded position. Support for agency regulation of pollution is a related issue; she did not address tort liability as an alternative.

voter-id.rationale: In 2021 she said 'of course people have to prove who they are' but warned ID rules could make that 'almost impossible' for rural voters; she backs the Freedom to Vote Act rather than strict ID mandates.

women-suffrage.rationale: Cites the women's suffrage struggle approvingly in her launch speech, as a case where those in power wrongly accused reformers of 'dividing the sexes'.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Says 'racism is real in America' and, in 2019, cited black women's maternal mortality, sentencing gaps and pay gaps as injustices that still hold people back.

notes: Living (born October 20, 1964; Wikipedia, checked 2026-10-23); she left the vice presidency on January 20, 2025 and declined to run for California governor in 2026. Views changed between 2019 and 2024: she backed a fracking ban and single-payer Medicare for All in 2019, then said in 2024 she would not ban fracking and no longer supports single payer; on illegal border crossing she said in 2024 'there should be consequence'. The most recent position is used where they differ. Her books (The Truths We Hold, 107 Days, Smart on Crime) could not be read in full; Senate roll calls and bill pages on congress.gov, govtrack.us and senate.gov returned access errors, so her votes and bills rest on the Wikipedia article on her political positions. The 2019 ACLU questionnaire was not reachable directly.
